The new generation Mac mini equipped with the M6 and M5 Pro chips officially launched this week, but we subsequently discovered three details that Apple did not specifically mention.

#1: Memory bandwidth varies by configuration

If you are planning to get a Mac mini, the ordering page actually does not fully list an important specification: memory bandwidth. Checking the technical specifications reveals that the RAM configuration you choose will directly affect the overall memory bandwidth.

The base model Mac mini equipped with the M6 chip comes with 16GB of RAM, providing 153GB/s of memory bandwidth. However, if you upgrade to 24GB or 32GB of RAM, the bandwidth jumps to 170GB/s.

In addition, to achieve the highest 307GB/s memory bandwidth, you must choose the M5 Pro version.

Each configuration has improvements compared to the M4 model, but the differences are worth noting.

#2: N1 chip adds Thread support

When Apple announced the new generation Mac mini, it highlighted support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, both upgrades compared to the Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 in the M4 model.

But looking at the technical specifications reveals that the M6 version of Mac mini has Apple's own N1 chip built in, and therefore also supports Thread.

Thread has been built into iPhones starting with the iPhone 15 Pro, and Apple has always touted its benefits for smart home accessories and automation. For the Mac mini, this is the first time this feature has been added.

#3: Pre-installed with macOS Golden Gate

If you are planning to hold off on upgrading to the new version of macOS for the time being, note that the M6 version of Mac mini comes pre-installed with macOS Golden Gate.

Apple did not explicitly mention this on its official website. However, the company reportedly confirmed to John Gruber that the new version of macOS has been pre-installed.

This situation is actually not unexpected, because the M6 version of Mac mini will not officially ship until September 22, while macOS 27 is expected to launch the week before (around September 14). However, users who have concerns about upgrading to new software should take note.

To get a full overview of all the new features of the M6 Mac mini compared to the M4 model, check back our complete roundup.

Starting today, you can pre-order the M6 and M5 Pro versions of the Mac mini, priced from $899 USD.

Are you planning to buy the M6 Mac mini? Feel free to let us know your reasons in the comments section.
